stem: Which choice best completes the researchers' explanation?
stimulus: Ornithologists noticed something odd about great tits living in a large city: their songs were higher in pitch than the songs of great tits in nearby forests. The researchers also measured the background sound in both places. Most city noise, such as the rumble of traffic, is low in pitch. The forests were quiet. The team hypothesizes that city birds sing higher because ______
choices: higher-pitched songs are easier to hear over the low rumble of traffic.
forest birds sing at a higher pitch than city birds do.
every bird species in the city has raised the pitch of its song.
city birds sing more at night, when the traffic is quietest.
explanation: The puzzle is the higher pitch in the city. The passage gives you one detail that explains it: city noise is low-pitched. A song pitched above that noise stands out from it, so this explanation uses both the observation and the measurement. You will use this same move on harder 'the team hypothesizes that' questions: find the detail the passage put there on purpose, and choose the answer that connects it to the puzzle.

B.why: You reversed the comparison. The passage says the city birds sang higher, not the forest birds.

C.why: The study looked at one species, great tits. Going from one species to every species is strength creep: the word 'every' claims far more than the passage supports.

D.why: This sounds like a scientific explanation, but it skips the key detail. The passage is about pitch and low-pitched noise, and it never mentions when the birds sing. This is the trap for this kind of question: an explanation that sounds sensible but ignores the clue.

stem: Which choice best completes the researchers' explanation?
stimulus: Folklorists recording tales in a mountain village were surprised to hear a detailed story about a sea serpent that drags fishing boats under the waves. The village is hundreds of miles from any coast, and none of the people living there today has ever fished at sea. However, church records show that the village was founded by families who had moved there from a fishing town. The folklorists hypothesize that the story ______
choices: was brought to the village by the families who founded it.
started in the village and later spread to the fishing town.
began when villagers saw a large creature in a mountain lake.
shows that all mountain folktales first came from the sea.
explanation: The puzzle is a sea story in a place far from the sea. The word 'However' brings in the detail that explains it: the founders came from a fishing town. If they carried the story with them, every fact in the passage makes sense. Harder hypothesis questions use the same pattern, where a contrast word introduces the clue that solves the puzzle.

B.why: You reversed the direction. The families moved from the fishing town to the village, so the story would have traveled the same way.

C.why: This is a believable origin story, but it ignores the church records, which are the key detail. It also fails to explain why the tale is about fishing boats and waves. This is the trap of picking an explanation that leaves out the clue.

D.why: The passage is about one story in one village. The word 'all' turns that single case into a rule the passage never supports.

stem: Which choice best completes the researchers' explanation?
stimulus: Many people assume that workers quit mainly because of low pay. One factory, however, puzzled labour economists: it paid more than any other factory in the region, yet its workers quit at twice the regional rate. The economists noted that it was also the only factory in the region that required workers to rotate between day and night shifts. They hypothesize that the workers quit mainly because ______
choices: they dislike having to switch between day and night shifts.
the factory pays them less than other factories in the region.
the higher pay lets the factory require rotating night shifts.
no worker will ever accept rotating shifts, whatever the pay.
explanation: The passage opens with the popular view, that pay drives quitting, and then undercuts it: this factory pays the most and still loses the most workers. The one thing that makes this factory different is rotating shifts, so that is the explanation that fits. When a passage sets up a popular view and then says 'however', the blank finishes the corrected view, not the original one.

B.why: You went back to the popular view the passage argues against. The factory pays more than the others, so low pay cannot explain why its workers quit.

C.why: This links the two details, but it explains the factory's policy rather than why workers quit, which is the question the passage asks.

D.why: Look at the words 'no worker' and 'ever'. The passage shows that more workers quit, not that every worker refuses. This is strength creep.

stem: Which choice best completes the researchers' explanation?
stimulus: Air usually gets colder as you climb a mountain, so the bottom of a valley is normally warmer than the slopes above it. On calm winter nights in one mountain valley, though, meteorologists found the opposite: the valley floor was several degrees colder than the slopes. Cold air is denser, and therefore heavier, than warm air. The meteorologists hypothesize that on calm nights, ______
choices: cold air sinks down the slopes and collects on the valley floor.
the air on the slopes is colder than the air on the valley floor.
the valley floor is colder than the slopes on every night of the year.
strong winds carry snow down from the slopes to the valley floor.
explanation: The usual pattern flips: the valley floor is colder, not warmer. The passage gives you the reason in its last fact. Cold air is heavy, so when there is no wind it slides downhill and pools at the bottom. This is the 'effect flips' version of a hypothesis question. Once the passage tells you the pattern reversed, your answer has to explain the reversal, not the usual pattern.

B.why: This is the usual pattern, which the passage says reversed on these nights. This is the trap for flipped-effect questions: choosing the original effect instead of its reverse.

C.why: The finding applies only to calm winter nights. 'Every night of the year' is strength creep that the passage does not support.

D.why: The passage says the nights were calm, so strong winds do not fit. This explanation also ignores the clue about dense, heavy cold air.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Palms are sensitive to cold: today they grow only in places where the ground rarely or never freezes. Many people would therefore be surprised to learn that paleobotanists have found fossilized palm fronds in 50-million-year-old rocks on an island off the coast of Antarctica. That island is now covered in ice for most of the year. To explain why palm fossils appear in such an unlikely place, the researchers hypothesize that ______
choices: palms living in the distant past could survive in places that stayed frozen for most of the year.
the island had a warm climate with little or no frost during the time when the palms were growing there.
the island was already covered in ice for most of the year during the time when the palms were growing there.
palms first appeared on this island and only later spread from there to warmer regions on other continents.
explanation: Start with the surprise: palms need ground that rarely or never freezes, yet their fossils turn up on an island that is icy today. Only one explanation fits every detail. When the palms were alive, the island must have been warm enough for them, so its climate has changed since then. This is the basic move behind every 'the researchers hypothesize that' question. Find the detail that doesn't fit, then choose the explanation that makes all the stated facts agree, without adding any new ones.

A.why: You picked an explanation that sounds scientific but drops the key detail. The passage says palms grow only where the ground rarely or never freezes. Saying ancient palms could survive a frozen climate goes against that fact. It doesn't solve the puzzle.

C.why: You took the island's present-day condition and applied it to the past. If the island had been icy 50 million years ago, cold-sensitive palms could not have grown there. That makes the puzzle worse instead of explaining it. The direction has to be that the island was warm then and is icy now.

D.why: You went past what the passage says. Nothing in it tells you where palms first appeared or how they spread. This choice also doesn't explain the puzzle, because a palm that started on the island would still need a warm climate to grow there.
